about: Every data op, at every place in a message it can name, in each direction: whether the compiler serves it, or blocks the release and why. A test builds a Change for every cell and checks the compiler does what the cell says, and fails if any cell is missing. Endpoint ops (route, retire, behavior) act on a whole operation and are listed once each.

body request.why: A schema scope reaches every request body that uses the schema.

body response.why: A schema scope reaches every response body that uses the schema, undone in reverse.

body outbound.why: A schema scope reaches every webhook and callback payload that uses the schema, undone in reverse as a response is, before the provider signs it.

cookie request.why: Cookies are addressed one by one; the rest of the Cookie header is kept as it came. A new kind of value in a union only reaches a caller in a response body, so `widen` is refused on a parameter.

cookie outbound.why: A payload the provider sends is a body; its parameters are the provider's own request to the subscriber, which no contract of the subscriber's describes.

cookie response.why: A response sets cookies with Set-Cookie, which no Change may touch.

header request.why: As for the query, with names compared case-insensitively. Credential, framing and signature headers, and any header the document's security schemes read, are refused: no Change may touch them. A new kind of value in a union only reaches a caller in a response body, so `widen` is refused on a parameter.

header outbound.why: A payload the provider sends is a body; its parameters are the provider's own request to the subscriber, which no contract of the subscriber's describes.

header response.why: The IR has no scope for response headers yet.

path request.why: A path parameter can be converted in place and is written back into the template. The template's parameters are fixed, so renaming, adding or removing one is a route change, and the gate blocks it as a parameter op. A path segment holds one value, so it cannot become a list or stop being one.

path outbound.why: A payload the provider sends is a body; its parameters are the provider's own request to the subscriber, which no contract of the subscriber's describes.

query request.why: A parameter scope reaches the operation's request envelope; each named query parameter is decoded and re-encoded in the style its declaration states, and every other one passes through byte for byte. A new kind of value in a union only reaches a caller in a response body, so `widen` is refused on a parameter.

query outbound.why: A payload the provider sends is a body; its parameters are the provider's own request to the subscriber, which no contract of the subscriber's describes.

route.why: The runtime routes an old caller's method and path to the new ones.

retire.why: The runtime answers 410 with the provider's guidance, and the provider never sees the call.

behavior.why: The runtime exposes the flag, and the provider branches on it in its own code.

inert.widen request: An old caller never sends a kind of value its contract does not describe, so nothing is translated on the way in; the op still says what the new contract accepts.
inert.relax request: A bound says which values are allowed; nothing is rewritten. A request bound that narrowed is refused at prediction, since old callers would be turned away.
inert.relax response: The value passes through as the API produced it; the loss is that an old caller may see a value its contract ruled out, which the provider acknowledges.
inert.relax outbound: As for a response: the payload's value passes through as the API produced it.
inert.convert dropValues response: A list an old caller is sent is the new contract's to fill, and holds none of the values it no longer has; nothing is taken out on the way back.
inert.convert dropValues outbound: As for a response: a payload's list is the new contract's to fill.
inert.restate request: The contract says the same values another way; nothing is rewritten, and the compiler refuses it unless every value an old caller sends is one the new contract accepts.
inert.restate response: The contract says the same values another way; nothing is rewritten, and the compiler refuses it unless every value the API now answers with is one the old contract allowed.
inert.restate outbound: As for a response: the compiler refuses it unless every payload the provider now sends is one the old contract allowed.
